summary: This class models a thermostat that remembers one temperature reading and reports what the heating system should be doing. Depending on how cold or warm it is, it answers "Heating", "Cooling", or "Idle".

lines.text: The temperature is stored as a double because thermostats deal in fractions of a degree, and `private` means only code inside this class can read or change it.
A constructor runs when someone creates a Thermostat, so every thermostat object starts life with a known temperature rather than a meaningless zero.
The parameter and the field share a name, so `this.currentTemp` makes clear that the field belongs to the object being built while the bare name refers to the value passed in.
This method is the whole point of the class: it turns a raw number into a word a person or a test can check.
Below 68 degrees the room is too cold, and returning immediately means the rest of the method never runs.
Because the first `return` already handled cold rooms, reaching this line means the temperature is at least 68, so only the upper limit needs checking.
Anything from 68 through 75 falls through both checks, so this is the comfortable middle range where the system does nothing.
